skill.name: skill-share
skill.description: Creates structured Claude skill packages, validates required metadata, and shares completed skills with a team through Slack.
skill.summary: Create, validate, package, and share team skills from one guided workflow.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The only static finding points to a fenced text example in SKILL.md, not executable Ruby or shell code. I found no evidence of prompt injection, credential access, or executable scripts in the reviewed file.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 67-73 are a fenced text example that describes expected skill creation steps. They do not contain Ruby backtick execution, shell commands, or executable code.

content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to create and distribute reusable AI skills. This skill guides creation, validation, packaging, and Slack sharing for faster discovery.
actual_capabilities: Creates skill directories with a SKILL.md template.
Generates scripts, references, and assets directories.
Checks required metadata and naming conventions.
Packages a completed skill as a distributable zip file.
Shares completed skills with a team through Slack.
limitations: It is a prompt-only skill with no included automation scripts.
Slack sharing requires the needed integration and permissions.
Generated skills still need human review before distribution.
It does not verify third-party license compatibility.

use_cases.title: Create internal assistant skills
use_cases.description: Build a consistent skill package for repeated team workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare reusable project tools
use_cases.description: Package references, scripts, and assets for a project-specific skill.

use_cases.title: Share approved skills
use_cases.description: Notify teammates when a new skill is ready for review or use.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill named meeting-notes. It should help summarize team meetings and list action items.

prompt_templates.title: Add complete metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for release note review. Include a clear description, author, version, license, and required folders.

prompt_templates.title: Validate before packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my new onboarding skill. Check the name, metadata, folder structure, and readiness for packaging.

prompt_templates.title: Package and announce
prompt_templates.prompt: Create, validate, package, and prepare a Slack announcement for a skill that audits support macros.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing release notes and share it with the platform team.
output: A skill folder is prepared with a clear name and metadata.
Required folders are included for scripts, references, and assets.
A package is prepared and a Slack share message is drafted.

output_examples.input: Validate my onboarding skill before I distribute it.
output: The review lists missing metadata, naming issues, and package readiness.
The final status explains what to fix before sharing.

best_practices: Use clear hyphen-case names that describe the skill purpose.
Review generated metadata before packaging or sharing.
Share only skills that have been tested with representative prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not package private credentials or internal secrets.
Do not share draft skills before required metadata is complete.
Do not rely on Slack sharing as a security approval step.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured skill folder with metadata and standard support directories.

faq.question: Does it include executable automation?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package only contains prompt instructions in SKILL.md.

faq.question: Can it package a skill for distribution?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes validation and zip packaging as part of the workflow.

faq.question: Does Slack sharing happen automatically?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for Slack sharing, but it depends on available integration access.

faq.question: Can it validate skill metadata?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks SKILL.md format, required fields, and naming conventions.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for team skill creation, internal tool packaging, and collaborative skill discovery.
